audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (second fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as twelve files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_b_<module>_1..3.json, three per module, split only so that each publishing call could carry complete literal content. Split 13 Paediatrics, 13 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 12 Psychiatry and 12 Medicine; tier mix 23 L3, 23 L4 and 4 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6542 with modules on 1636, 1636, 1635 and 1635. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed all four modules exactly level on 1623, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.83 points in Paediatrics, 13.40 in Obstetrics, 12.60 in Medicine and 11.61 in Psychiatry, and L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 13.27, 12.77, 11.79 and 10.74 respectively, while L5 sat at 4.99 per cent in every module, a deficit of about 0.01 points. As on the previous nine fires the strict per question argmax is degenerate: it would pour the whole batch into the single largest deficit cell, Paediatrics L3, and breach the Section 2 requirement that the four modules stay within about 10 of each other. This fire therefore allocated 13/13/12/12, which keeps the module spread at 1 and follows the tie break clause toward the lower count modules, and within each module it followed the ideal tier shape rather than the raw argmax because L3 leads L4 by under one point everywhere and a pure L3 batch would immediately reopen the L4 deficit. One L5 per module holds that tier at 5.01 per cent rather than letting it decay, which is the same reasoning recorded on the 2026-09-16 a fire. The structural point for the maintainer still stands: because L5 sits close to target its deficit can never exceed the 11 to 14 point deficits carried by L3 and L4, so a strict argmax reading will never select an L5 cell and the tier needs an explicit per batch quota if sustained growth is wanted. Audit: valid JSON, zero em-dashes and zero non-ASCII characters, zero banned tokens, every question difficulty 3, 4 or 5, answer-length parity max to min at or under 1.35 on all 50, correct letters exactly 10 per letter A to E, source_refs all resolving to declared source labels, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, reference_ranges keys all valid, vitals in fixed order or compressed to within normal limits, data_table values all flat strings, no lead-in guideline leak, no parenthetical qualifier in any correct option, no correct option uniquely carrying a numeral, no weight-based dose arithmetic in any lead-in, explanation.summary 3 to 5 sentences with 3 to 5 key points and a specific pearl on every question. Four defects were found on audit and fixed before publication: a placeholder left in the model field of the venous leg ulcer item; a correct option uniquely carrying a numeral in the microscopic colitis item, corrected by adding doses to two distractors; an option parity ratio of 1.409 in the chronic lymphocytic leukaemia item, corrected by lengthening the correct option; and a six sentence explanation summary in the Q fever item. Correct letter distribution was rebalanced in the Obstetrics and Medicine files by swapping option positions. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new was run against the 6492 pre-existing questions and PASSED on the first run with zero duplicates, and intra-batch self comparison returned zero pairs at or above 0.62; both checks were repeated against the published files after the push and passed again. No threshold was altered and the script was not modified. The clean first pass reflects a pre-generation coverage probe that screened about 260 candidate topics against the existing bank and discarded roughly forty already covered, among them toddler's diarrhoea, narcolepsy with cataplexy, postpartum thyroiditis, anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, cardiac amyloidosis, heparin induced thrombocytopenia, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, valproate hyperammonaemic encephalopathy, habit reversal for trichotillomania, nicotine replacement in pregnancy, Bell palsy, trigeminal neuralgia and gestational diabetes screening after bariatric surgery.
